subject: Renewal conversation: staged SLA upgrade and capacity runway for Nimbus Health
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@nimbushealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: rachel+procure@nimbushealth.com
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning — premium SLA and capacity runway

Hi Aisha,

Our annual renewal for Redwood is coming up in December and we want to discuss a couple of items before signing:

- We plan to increase Q1 query volume by ~2.5x due to a new rollout.
- Recently we've seen tail latency spikes on critical routes during peak; we need improved latency guarantees and faster incident response (on-call + P1 escalation).
- We're interested in a premium support tier with a short trial period so we can validate both latency and operational handoff.

Could you share what a staged upgrade would look like (trial → dedicated reservation), pricing ranges, and an outline of the SLOs and credits? Also need any procurement/legal artifacts (addendum or redlines) we can circulate.

Thanks — let's aim for a planning call next week.

Ethan
CTO, Nimbus Health

Attachments: none

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: rachel+procure@nimbushealth.com
Date: 2026-10-26T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — premium SLA and capacity runway

Hi Ethan — thanks for the clear ask. We can run a "phased premium upgrade" that minimizes risk while validating latency and operational handoffs. High level proposal: 

Phase A (90-day Trial)
- Enabled premium support on your production account for 90 days (P1/24x7 + 1-hour P1 ack, 2-hour P1 mitigation SLA).
- Canary routing on two critical endpoints (your inference-heavy routes) to validate tail latency improvements.
- Dedicated on-call rotation with a named escalation engineer.

Phase B (Commit)
- Option to convert to a 12-month Dedicated Capacity reservation with a 10% unit-rate discount and a guaranteed burst runway (20% additional capacity for the first quarter).
- Addendum will include updated latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99 targets by route), credits for missed SLOs, and onboarding milestones.

Operational notes: to meet p99 tail targets we recommend prefix KV caching + per-route batching. We'll include recommended model variants and quantization settings in the addendum. Estimated lead time for dedicated pool: ~4 weeks from signed commit.

I've attached a first-pass addendum and a short forecast worksheet — can you review? If that looks sensible I can schedule a 30-minute call with engineering and your procurement to go through SLO language and pricing.

Proposed next steps:
1) You review attachments and confirm required SLO thresholds.
2) Call next Tue 10/31 or Wed 11/1 — propose Tue 10:30 PT.
3) If approved, we issue a DocuSign addendum for signature and kick off the 90-day trial during the uptake week.

Regards,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Premium_SLA_Trial_Addendum_v1.pdf, Q4_Forecast_Nimbus.xlsx

From: rachel+procure@nimbushealth.com
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — premium SLA and capacity runway

Hi Aisha — thanks. A few questions from procurement/legal before the call: 

- Can you clarify credit calculation for p99 misses (is it per-route or aggregate across account)?
- Is the 90-day trial refundable/terminable without penalty if targets are not met?
- Need SOC2 Type II evidence and retention policy summary for audit.

Also — can you provide a short runbook that describes the on-call escalation path and who will be the named engineer? We'll need that to get internal approval for the pilot.

Best,
Rachel
VP, Procurement (Nimbus Health)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Nimbus renewal — request for quick technical/pricing alignment (internal)

Folks — Nimbus (CTO + procurement) wants a staged SLA upgrade with a 90-day trial, then option to convert to a 12mo reserved pool. Questions from procurement: credit calculation per-route vs aggregate, trial termination terms, and SOC2 evidence. They also asked for an on-call runbook and a named escalation engineer.

Ask: can someone confirm the following items so I can get back to them by EOD 11/4?
- Marcus: technical approach / visible levers to hit p99 tail latency for their critical routes (KV caching, batching, model variant recommendations) and any lead-time constraints. Also cost impact on unit price if we require a specific quantized variant.
- Monica: pricing for 90-day trial (should trial be free or bill at reduced rate? propose a credit bridge?) and the 12-month committed pricing with the 10% discount (model a ballpark).
- Lauren: legal template for the addendum, suggested language for credit calculation (per-route or account-level) and trial termination clause. Also provide SOC2 artifact location or pointer.

Timeline: call with Nimbus scheduled 2026-11-04 10:30 PT.

Thanks — Aisha

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T12:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Nimbus renewal — request for quick technical/pricing alignment (internal)

Quick notes from infra side:

- To reliably meet aggressive p99 tail numbers on inference routes we should:
  * Enable prefix/KV caching for warm sessions (saves ~30-50% tail latency on long chains).
  * Configure continuous batching with an upper latency cap per route; this reduces cost per token but needs route-specific settings.
  * Recommend nq-quant variant for their larger models — slightly higher memory but lower inference compute and better latency stability.

- Lead time: enabling the trial (premium support, canary routing, named on-call) -> 3 business days.
- Dedicated capacity pool lead time: ~4 weeks (provision GPUs, run repro files, validate kernels).
- Cost impact: if we lock them to nq-quant variant across mission-critical routes, estimate +8% on unit price but with 20% fewer compute seconds due to optimized kernels — net should still be favorable vs hosted burst.
- Credits: we can do per-route credits for missed SLOs (clearer for both parties) but need to limit to top 5 routes to avoid attribution complexity.

I can draft a short runbook for the named engineer and provide the engineering contact for the trial.

Marcus
Senior Product Manager, Runtime

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@nimbushealth.com>, rachel+procure@nimbushealth.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T16:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — staged SLA addendum and next steps

Hi Ethan / Rachel — thanks for your patience. Following our internal alignment we've attached an updated addendum and a short runbook. Summary of changes: 

- Trial: 90-day Premium Support trial (starts on activation date) — trial is terminable with 14-day notice; no early-termination fee for the trial window.
- SLOs: per-route p50/p95/p99 targets included in Appendix A (we suggested top-5 routes to keep attribution simple).
- Credits: per-route credit schedule for missed p99 targets; capped to 5% of monthly invoice per route and aggregated cap 12%/month.
- Conversion: if Nimbus converts to a 12-month Dedicated Capacity reservation within 30 days after trial end, they receive a 10% unit-rate discount and a 20% burst runway applied during the first 90 days post-conversion.
- On-call: named escalation engineer and a 1-hour P1 acknowledgement target during trial. Runbook attached.
- SOC2: pointer to SOC2 Type II artifact + retention summary included in the addendum.

Attachments: Premium_SLA_Trial_Addendum_v1.pdf (updated), Q4_Forecast_Nimbus.xlsx, redwood-sla-examples.csv
DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/ol/contract/abc123-sign

Next steps:
1) Please review and provide any redline requests by EOD 11/24.
2) If agreeable I will send the DocuSign for signatures and we will schedule the trial activation call (30 minutes) for the week after signature.

Happy to hop on a call if you want to walk the addendum line-by-line.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Premium_SLA_Trial_Addendum_v1.pdf, redwood-sla-examples.csv
